name: AgentMsgr
pricing: Free $0: up to 3 agents, 1 group chat, 100 messages a day, 250 MB for files, full message history, installable on an iPhone home screen. Pro: $10.49 a month at launch against a $29.99 list price (the '65% off' badge checks out - 29.99 x 0.35 = 10.49), unlimited agents and group chats, 150 messages an hour and 3,000 a week, 5 GB for files. Only messages you type count; agents' replies do not. Paid through Stripe checkout in the app or arranged directly, cancelled from Manage billing, with Pro running to the end of the paid period. A Teams tier is shown as 'Later' and is not sold. USD; no card for the free plan. Verified 2026-11-13.
best_for: People who already pay for agents on more than one platform - a Grok Bot agent, a Meta Muse agent, a ChatGPT dot, Claude, Hermes, OpenClaw, or a bot they built themselves - and want them in one thread that can work on the same task instead of five apps. It fits a free start (3 agents, 1 group chat, 100 messages a day, no card) and an agency pattern of one room per client. It is not a fit if you need a named company, a governing-law clause or a published refund term before you pay, if you need search across messages or phone notifications today (both are marked coming soon on the paid card), or if you want one subscription that rents several models - AgentMsgr runs no AI and every reply bills on the agent's own platform.
summary: AgentMsgr is a messaging app for AI agents you already run elsewhere. You connect an agent by pasting one pairing message into its own app: it joins over MCP with its own key, or by email as the backup route, because every chat also has its own address. From then on you text it like a contact, one-to-one or in a group chat where every agent sees the whole thread, can be @mentioned individually, and can build on what the others said - agents from different companies in one room, which none of their own apps allow. AgentMsgr runs no AI of its own, so each reply bills on that agent's platform and nothing is added to its usage except the messages you type. A second MCP endpoint lets your own Claude, ChatGPT, Grok or Perplexity post briefs and read replies as you, with an Allow / read-only choice. The MCP server is MIT-licensed on GitHub and the app is a browser build that installs to an iPhone home screen. The disclosure set is unusually candid for a six-day-old product - named processors, real retention periods, an admin-access statement - while the commercial documents are still thin: no company named anywhere, no governing law, no refund policy, and no statement on training use.

name: BotLoadout
pricing: Free (97 templates; no paid tier, sponsorship-funded)
best_for: Starting a first Claude, ChatGPT or Grok agent from a worked template instead of writing the system prompt, connectors and setup from scratch
summary: A free library of 97 AI agent templates, each published in separate Claude, ChatGPT and Grok versions with the system prompt, the connectors to switch on, a short setup sequence, an example input and output, and stated limits. The full prompt text is public and there is no hosted runtime: the templates are copied into your own account, and the site is funded by newsletter sponsorship rather than subscriptions.

name: Catch
pricing: $99/month billed monthly (10-day free trial; cancel anytime)
best_for: Busy executives who want an AI admin to schedule meetings, triage email, book travel, and make calls
summary: An AI admin assistant that schedules meetings, drafts email, books travel, and places phone calls over Slack, Messages, email, or voice — positioned as action-taking rather than suggest-or-summarize.

name: CustomGPT.ai

Premium $499/month or $449/month billed annually (25 agents, 5,000 queries/month, 20,000 documents per agent, 300 million words, 5 seats, auto-sync, branding removal). Enterprise custom. Every published plan starts with a 7-day trial that requires a credit card and then charges the selected plan. Checked 2026-10-27.
best_for: a no-code agent on their own documents, with a published query cap and a document limit, who can judge answer quality during the 7-day card-required trial
summary: CustomGPT.ai sells no-code agents built on a customer's own documents. The pricing page checked on 2026-10-27 lists Standard at $99/month ($89 billed annually) and Premium at $499/month ($449 billed annually), plus a custom Enterprise plan. Both published tiers start with a 7-day trial that requires a credit card and charges the selected plan when the trial ends. This listing records those published limits. It does not treat the affiliate approval as a product score, and no hands-on result is published.

summary: An open-source autonomous agent framework from Nous Research with tools, skills, memory, profiles, messaging gateways, delegation, MCP, and scheduled routines.

name: Markin
pricing: Monthly subscriptions in EUR plus VAT, sold through a request form rather than a checkout, with a free tier. Free: EUR 0 for 200 one-off welcome credits that expire 30 calendar days after they are granted, no card and no automatic charge, but access is requested rather than signed up. Pro at four capacity tiers: EUR 49/month for 750 credits, EUR 149/month for 2,500, EUR 490/month for 8,500 and EUR 990/month for 17,500, credits shared by the whole team with no per-seat fee. Annual billing is a 20% discount over twelve monthly payments, paid once for the year, with the credits still granted monthly rather than all at once; no annual figure is published anywhere on the page, so the discounted total has to be computed from the monthly price. Unused credits roll over into one additional monthly period and expire at the end of it, oldest credits consumed first; cancelling a monthly plan runs to the end of the paid month, and cancelling an annual plan stops renewal while access and the monthly credit grants continue to the end of the paid year. Enterprise is custom - agreed capacity, tailored integrations, a forward deployed engineer, DPA and security review, adapted invoicing. The pricing FAQ states 'there is no online checkout yet' and that the team confirms access, configuration and billing before anything is charged. No purchase was attempted.
best_for: D2C growth, CRM or lifecycle teams sitting on a large customer base and an existing stack (Shopify, Klaviyo, Braze, Salesforce, a warehouse) who want an agent system to find revenue opportunities, size them and run holdout-measured experiments - rather than another dashboard or another set of segments to build by hand
summary: Markin is an agentic growth platform for large direct-to-consumer businesses. You connect a store, CRM and warehouse; its agents read customer behaviour, propose revenue opportunities with a size attached, prepare or launch the intervention in the tools you already run, and read each result against a control group. The pitch is deliberately narrow - incremental ARPU, not more dashboards - and the vendor is unusually candid on its own comparison page that an LLM wired to your data through MCP can do parts of this work; what it sells is the assembled system, the experiment bookkeeping, the audit trail and the team that stands behind it. Access is sales-led: the free allowance and every paid plan begin with a request form, and the pricing FAQ says outright that there is no online checkout yet.

summary: An open-source multi-channel gateway for AI agents that can run on your own infrastructure and connect conversations, tools, and model providers.

best_for: Resolving customer support tickets end to end across email, chat, voice and WhatsApp with AI agents that act inside the helpdesk you already run
summary: An AI customer support platform whose agents work tickets rather than only answering them: they read the systems an answer lives in, act through tools built from your APIs, and hand anything they cannot finish to a person with the checking already done. It runs inside an existing helpdesk or standalone with its own inbox.

name: TypingMind
pricing: Free + paid plans
best_for: Self-hosted multi-model chat with unified prompts and model routing
summary: A self-hostable chat interface that unifies multiple LLM providers under one prompt library and usage dashboard.

name: AccurateScribe.ai
pricing: Free tier: partial transcripts and basic features, no card. One paid plan, unlimited: $9.99/month billed annually at $119.99/year, or $19.99 month-to-month; both cards advertise unlimited transcription, files up to 10 hours each, speaker identification and 134+ languages. USD; PayPal shown on the pricing page. Verified 2026-11-09 on /pricing and on the /ar/pricing locale mirror, which carries the same three figures ($9.99, $119.99, $19.99).
best_for: Solo transcribers, podcasters, journalists, students and small teams who want one flat unlimited plan instead of a minutes meter - $9.99 a month billed yearly or $19.99 monthly, 134+ languages, speaker identification, subtitles and DOCX/PDF/SRT export, free to try on partial transcripts. A good fit if you transcribe a few hours a week and would rather not track a credit balance. Not a fit if you need a named counterparty or governing law before you pay, if you expect any refund after purchase (the policy is non-refundable even if the service is unused), or if you need a per-minute rate for very high volume - the same operator's WhisperTranscribe.ai and WhisperTranscript.ai brands sell meters, both of which are held pending verification rather than listed.
summary: AccurateScribe.ai is a transcription and subtitle service that turns audio or video into text in 134+ languages, with speaker identification, SRT/VTT subtitle output and export to DOCX, PDF, TXT and CSV. Its commercial model is unusually simple for this class: a free tier that returns partial transcripts, then one unlimited plan at $9.99 a month billed yearly ($119.99) or $19.99 month-to-month, rather than the minutes-metered ladders most competitors sell. The product has been live since November 2024 and is distributed well beyond the website - a docs subdomain, an iOS app, a Chrome extension, a Microsoft Store listing, a ChatGPT app and a Google Workspace add-on - and its privacy policy is unusually specific about the parts that matter: original uploads are deleted after processing, extracted audio is kept 30 days, transcripts stay under the account holder's control, and it states that recordings and transcripts are not used to train its own or third parties' models and are not human-reviewed. What the site does not say is who runs it: no company, postal address, jurisdiction or governing-law clause appears on any page, the refund policy is 'final and non-refundable, regardless of whether the service has been used', and the pricing page runs a permanent countdown on a 'New Customer Offer' alongside a corporate-logo band it describes as customers.

best_for: browser speech enhancement and short studio sessions with a published free plan
summary: Adobe's browser podcast tools for Enhance Speech cleanup and Studio recording. The official plans page publishes a Free plan and a Premium plan with a 30-day free trial. Exact Premium US-dollar pricing was not listed on that page during this check, so no unofficial third-party dollar figure is recorded.

summary: An editor that lets creators edit audio and video by editing text, with AI cleanup and production features.

best_for: AI voice generation, dubbing, narration, and voice agents
summary: A leading AI voice platform for realistic speech, narration, dubbing, and voice product experiences.

name: MeloLetter
pricing: One-time or monthly subscription, USD. $19.90 per song pack (one-time, no subscription) or $9.90/month for three song packs a month, renewing monthly. One song pack = two generated song versions plus one included regenerate, MP3 downloads and a shareable gift page. A lyric draft and a 30-second audio preview of both versions are free before payment, subject to rolling 24-hour limits and daily capacity. The same $19.90 and $9.90 figures appear on /pricing and on the /zh pricing page. Refunds are a single Terms clause rather than a policy page ('payments are not automatically refundable after generation work has started or a paid credit has been used'). No purchase was attempted.
best_for: People buying a one-off keepsake gift - a birthday, an anniversary, a proposal, a thank-you to a parent or friend - who want to hear and read the thing before they pay for it, and who would rather spend $19.90 once than hold a music-generation subscription they will use twice a year
summary: MeloLetter turns a written story - names, memories, the things you meant to say - into a personalised song gift. You answer guided prompts, get an AI lyric draft you can edit before paying, hear a free 30-second preview of both generated versions, and then buy a song pack to unlock full playback, MP3 downloads and a public shareable gift page. Songs come from Suno v5.5 through the YourMusic API and lyrics from GPT-5.5 through Brioi, both named with model identifiers in the terms. It sells one pack at $19.90 or three a month at $9.90. What stands out for a four-month-old site is documentation: the privacy policy names its analytics stack with retention periods, the terms carry a usable acceptable-use policy with a moderation and appeals process, and the examples page labels its demos 'illustrative' instead of dressing them as customer stories. What is missing is who runs it - no company, individual, postal address or governing law - and there is no refund page, only that clause.

summary: A remote recording studio for podcasts and video shows. Writing tools (lyrics, titles, prompts) cost no song credits, and the same credit balance is exposed through a remote MCP server and an OpenAPI-described REST API plus CLI.

name: AI Image to Prompt
pricing: Free, with no paid tier for this tool: the homepage, FAQ, Terms and llms.txt all describe it as free to use with no account, no download and no credit card. Note that the site's own /pricing route does not describe this product - it still serves the ShipAny SaaS-boilerplate price list (Starter $99/mo or $89/mo billed annually for 100 credits, Standard $199 or $169 for 200, Premium $299 or $249 for 300, each 'Get ShipAny' and bundling a NextJS boilerplate, Supabase storage and Vercel deploy), and /zh/pricing carries the same ladder in Chinese, while /docs serves ShipAny's own developer documentation. The tool itself takes no payment. Verified 2026-11-12 on /, /pricing, /zh/pricing, /privacy-policy, /terms-of-service, /llms.txt, /sitemap.xml and /docs.
best_for: Creators and small teams who already have a reference image and need a written brief for it: illustrators testing an art direction, designers producing concept variants, marketers fixing a campaign's visual language from a moodboard, and hobbyists learning how image prompts are structured. It fits the free-and-anonymous case well - no account, eight output languages, model-specific formatting for Midjourney, Stable Diffusion, Flux and Nano Banana - and it fits someone who wants one editable paragraph rather than four variants at once. It is a poor fit if you need to know who operates the site, what law governs it, or what anything costs: there is no company, controller, postal address or named jurisdiction anywhere, the only address published is a personal Gmail, the pricing page belongs to a different product, and six five-star testimonials from named people carry no evidence they are real.
summary: AI Image to Prompt is a free browser tool that reads an uploaded image and writes the text prompt that would recreate something like it, formatted for the image model you name. You supply a JPG, PNG or WebP up to 8MB by drag-and-drop, file picker, clipboard paste or public image URL, pick an output style (General, Nano Banana, Flux, Midjourney with comma-separated descriptors and parameters, or Stable Diffusion with tags and a suggested negative prompt), and optionally an output language from eight options, then copy an editable result. A text-to-prompt mode handles the same job without an image, and a prompt history is kept in the browser. No account is required and the site says uploads are deleted after processing, with generation run through kie.ai on Cloudflare infrastructure. It describes visible elements - subject, setting, composition, perspective, lighting, palette, style, mood - and the site is explicit that it does not recover the original hidden prompt behind an AI image, only a reproduction-oriented approximation. Verification was read-only: the /api/generate route is live and rejects an empty body with 400 {"error":"no_image"}, but no generation was run, so output quality is not assessed here.

summary: Adobe’s generative AI suite for images, text effects, edits, and creative production within the Adobe ecosystem.

summary: A fuse-bead pattern generator: upload a photo or describe a subject and it produces a bead grid matched to Perler, Hama, Artkal, MARD and COCO palettes with per-colour bead counts, printable PDF and PNG export, and a browser-side editor. Photo conversion is free and costs no credits.

name: Change Text in Image
pricing: One-time credit packs, USD, no subscription: Starter $14.90 for 400 credits (40 text edits, $0.37 per edit), Pro $26.90 for 1,000 credits (100 edits, $0.27), Studio $39.90 for 1,800 credits (180 edits, $0.22). Each generation costs 10 credits and new accounts get 10 free credits, which is one free edit. Credits do not expire while the account remains available, failed generations return the credits spent, and checkout runs through Waffo Pancake as merchant of record. The same figures and the same per-edit arithmetic render on the /zh mirror. Verified 2026-11-18 on /#pricing, /zh and /api/config/public.
best_for: Creators, e-commerce sellers and small marketing teams who need to change words already baked into a finished image - a typo on an exported ad, a price on a product shot, a date on an invitation, a label in a screenshot - without the source file, priced per edit at 10 credits with a one-time pack instead of a subscription. Also worth a look if you want a text-blur tool that provably runs on your own device. Not a fit if you need a named company and jurisdiction before paying, if you need account password recovery, if you need a committed deletion deadline for uploaded images, or if you are editing IDs, receipts, bank statements or other evidence (banned in its own acceptable-use policy).
summary: Change Text in Image does one narrow job and does it in a browser: you upload a JPG, PNG or static WebP up to 10MB / 20MP, drag a box over the words you want to replace, type the original text and the replacement, and the model redraws the wording in the font, colour and style it detected while rebuilding the background behind the old letters. Leaving the replacement empty removes the text instead. There are no font, size or colour controls, by design - the promise is an edit that looks like it was always there - and the neighbouring pages cover the same workflow for screenshots and translations, plus a blur tool that runs entirely on your device. Pricing is one-time credit packs only: $14.90 for 40 edits, $26.90 for 100 and $39.90 for 180, with 10 free credits at sign-up. The paperwork is unusually straight for this class - the operators are named as an individual with a working contact, Cloudflare, fal.ai's Nano Banana and Waffo are named by company and function, prompt screening before generation is disclosed, and the policy refuses to claim zero retention or supplier-wide no-training. What holds it back is that it says tracking is not active while Google Analytics, Microsoft Clarity and a third-party visitor counter all load on the policy page itself, and that no company, address or jurisdiction appears anywhere.

name: Copy.ai
pricing: Free + paid plans
best_for: Go-to-market workflows, sales copy, and repeatable marketing content systems
summary: An AI platform for marketing and sales content workflows, from copy generation to GTM process support.

name: DREAMMMER
pricing: Subscriptions, monthly or yearly: Starter $29/mo for 1,500 credits ($20.30/mo on the $243.60 yearly plan), Pro $99/mo for 6,000 credits ($59.40/mo on $712.80 yearly), Studio $299/mo for 18,000 credits plus 1,000 free 1K/2K images a month on any model ($149.50/mo on $1,794 yearly). One-time credit pack: 60,000 credits for $999, never expires. 50 free sign-up credits, one time, no card. Subscription credits expire when the next monthly allowance arrives and do not roll over; pack credits and the 1,000-credit first-subscription gift never expire. Failed or refused generations are refunded in credits automatically. USD before local tax; Waffo (merchant of record) or PayPal. Verified 2026-11-09 on /pricing and /api/config/public.
best_for: Marketers, designers and small teams who want one subscription that reaches GPT Image, Nano Banana, Seedream, Qwen, Grok, Kling, Veo, Seedance and MiniMax models without buying each one - an agent writes the prompt and picks the model, 50 free sign-up credits, then $29-$299 a month or a $999 one-time pack. Not a fit if you need a named company or a governing-law clause before you pay, if you expect work made on the free tier to stay private (it can be published in the showcase with its prompts and reference images), or if you need subscription credits to roll over month to month.
summary: DREAMMMER is a browser AI image and video editor built around an agent rather than a model picker: you describe the result, it writes the English prompt, chooses among GPT Image 2.5, Nano Banana 2.1, Seedream 5.0, Qwen Image 3.0, Grok Imagine, Kling 3.0, Veo 3.1, Seedance 2.5 and MiniMax H3, and you refine in the same thread while every step is mapped on a canvas. Eleven one-click tools (background remove, upscale, object remover, photo restore, clothes and background changer, expand) sit in front of the same credit meter, and a public showcase publishes real prompts with the model and credit cost behind each result. The commercial terms are unusually clear for a four-month-old product: you own what you create, the site states it does not train its own models on your uploads, failed generations refund credits automatically, and there is a written 7-day refund window with a 20% usage cap. What is missing is identity and data detail rather than honesty: no registered company is named anywhere, there is no governing-law clause, the policy promises to say how long data is kept and never gives a period, and Google Analytics loads on the privacy policy itself while the policy names no analytics vendor.

name: Edit Pic Text
pricing: Subscriptions, monthly: Basic $11.90/mo for 100 credits, Standard $29.90/mo for 300, Pro $79.90/mo for 1,050. Yearly, billed as $118.80 / $238.80 / $358.80 and shown as $9.90 / $19.90 / $29.90 a month (the plan config carries 1,800 / 4,800 / 10,800 credits for the year, which is a different allowance from the monthly cards - ask before choosing yearly). One-time credit packs, valid 183 days: Lite $9.90 for 80 credits, Core $19.90 for 150, Plus $29.90 for 250, Max $39.90 for 400, up to $199 for 2,500. A $4.99 Starter Pass carries 40 credits for 7 days. One edit, translation or enhance costs 5 credits (1K); text extraction costs 1. Free: 3 credits at sign-up plus a daily check-in ladder (3/3/6/3/3/3/9) totalling 30, which is what the 'Get 30 credits for free' badge counts. USD; the Chinese mirror prices the same three plans at CNY 87 / 219 / 583 a month. Verified 2026-11-15 on /pricing, /zh/pricing and the served plan config.
best_for: Creators, ecommerce and small marketing teams who need to change words that are already baked into an image - fixing a typo on an exported flyer, updating a price on a product shot, relabelling UI copy in a screenshot - without the original design file, at 5 credits per edit with the cost shown before you send. Also worth a look if you need text extraction (1 credit) or image translation in the same place. Not a fit if you need the vendor to name the company you are paying, if you are editing identity documents or payment screenshots (banned in its own terms), or if you want a vendor whose pricing page describes only the product it sells.
summary: Edit Pic Text rewrites the words already inside a picture instead of laying new text on top: you upload a JPG, PNG or WebP up to 30MB, the editor outlines the text it detects, you type the replacement - or leave it blank to remove the words - and the result comes back with the surrounding typeface, weight and background redrawn so the edit does not look pasted on. Instructions in plain English ('keep the logo', 'match the bold style') steer harder edits, and exports go to 1K, 2K or 4K. Four sibling pages cover the jobs people actually search for - screenshot text editing, OCR-style extraction that keeps headings and tables, translation into 110 languages with the original layout, and sharpening blurry text - each with a Chinese mirror. The workflow is honest about cost (5 credits per edit, shown before you send) and about limits (IDs, passports, receipts and payment screenshots are refused). What keeps it below the rest of the catalog is the paperwork around the product: the pricing page's comparison table prices video models this site does not sell, the same table charges 3 credits for an edit the editor bills at 5, the FAQ says refunds stop at 50 used credits while the refund policy says 10, and no company, address or jurisdiction is named anywhere.

name: Faceloria
pricing: Free instant face-shape analysis with basic measurements. Full Face Report $16.99 one-time (site states 'One-time payment - No subscription'), processed by Waffo. Verified 2026-11-02 on /pricing.
best_for: People curious about face-shape analysis who want a structured facial-measurement report rather than a horoscope-style app: upload one front-facing photo, get a face-shape category, width-to-height ratio and vertical-balance measurements for free, then decide whether the $16.99 one-time Full Report (4-week styling action plan and PDF) is worth it. Not a fit for anyone who needs a named company, jurisdiction or refund policy before paying, or for anyone who finds a 0-100 attractiveness score unhelpful - that framing is part of the product.
summary: Faceloria runs an AI face analysis in the browser: you upload a front-facing photo and get a face-shape category, symmetry and proportion measurements, plus an optional one-time Full Report with a styling action plan. The pitch leans on a 0-100 'attractiveness score' alongside the geometry, and the site itself frames results as informational. The operation is unusually transparent about the data path for a face tool: payments are handled by Waffo, source photos sit in Cloudflare R2 and are automatically deleted within 48 hours, and a complete legal set (privacy, terms, cookie and acceptable-use pages) is in place with a recent update date. The weak spots are identity and analytics: no company, controller or governing law is named anywhere, and the pages load a Plausible-compatible analytics script from pvuv.ai while the privacy policy says only that analytics 'run only when enabled by deployment configuration'.

name: Ideogram

name: ImagesV2
pricing: Free: 3 credits on sign-up (the first image costs 3 instead of 10). Yearly: Starter $49.90/yr (12,000 credits, ~$4.16/mo), Pro $199.90/yr (60,000, ~$16.66/mo), Ultra $499.90/yr (240,000, ~$41.66/mo). Monthly: Starter $8.40 (list $14.90, 1,000 credits), Pro $33.90 (list $39.90, 5,000), Ultra $84.90 (list $99.90, 20,000). One-time packs, credits never expire: Taster $9.90 (500 credits), Starter $39.90 (5,000), Pro $99.90 (20,000), Max $199.90 (50,000). No free trial on paid plans; all purchases final and non-refundable.
best_for: Designers, marketers and e-commerce sellers who need finished image assets - posters with readable text, true transparent PNGs, editable SVG and layered PSD - from OpenAI's GPT Image 2 without an OpenAI account, and who would rather buy credits than add another monthly AI subscription
summary: A browser image studio built around OpenAI's GPT Image 2, with GPT Image 2.5, GPT Image 1.5/1 and the Nano Banana family switchable behind one credits wallet. Instead of a blank prompt box it ships finished workflows: poster and infographic generation, transparent-background PNGs, editable text and SVG vector export, poster-to-layered-PSD conversion, photo restoration, 360 panoramas, brand kits, app mockups, article illustrations, portrait restyling and a set of social-screenshot generators. Generation costs are shown on the button before you spend - 10 credits per image at Low, 40 at Medium, 110 at High, plus 10 for transparent SVG or PSD output and 20 for image-to-image. You can subscribe or buy credit packs that never expire; either way no OpenAI account or ChatGPT Plus is needed.

name: Jasper
pricing: Paid plans
best_for: Marketing content workflows, brand voice, and campaign production
summary: A marketing-focused AI writing platform for brand voice, campaign assets, and content operations.

name: LayerGrab
pricing: Freemium. Subscriptions: Basic $12/month for 1,200 credits (~120 layers), Premium $36/month for 3,600 credits (~450 layers), yearly billing saves 31%. One-time credit packs: $20 for 1,800 credits, $60 for 6,600 credits (pack credits expire - see their FAQ). Each image-to-layers split costs 10 credits on Basic, 8 on Premium. Verified 2026-11-02 on /pricing.
best_for: Designers, ecommerce sellers and social-media editors who need to pull one element off a flat image - a product, a poster's text, a sticker - as a clean transparent layer without opening desktop software. The Chrome extension (right-click any image on the web) is the fastest version of the job. Not a fit for anyone who needs a named company and a refund policy before paying, or for bulk API automation (no developer API is offered).
summary: LayerGrab splits a flat image into editable, named layers with AI: upload or right-click an image, get each element (text, products, graphics) on its own transparent layer with the background filled in behind them, and export PNG, ZIP or a layered PSD. It works in the browser, a Chrome extension (listed on the Chrome Web Store), and - per its privacy page - Photoshop, Figma and Sketch plugins. The credit math is spelled out with worked examples on the pricing page (a 10-layer poster at 10 credits per layer on Basic costs $1.10). The gaps are identity and consumer paperwork: no company or jurisdiction is named anywhere, there is no refund policy page and no contact page, and the AI model doing the splitting is described only as 'our processing partner'.

name: Leonardo AI
pricing: Free + paid plans
best_for: Game assets, concept art, product mockups, and controlled image generation
summary: A creative AI platform for image generation, asset production, style control, and visual experimentation.

name: Makify AI
pricing: Free: 30 sign-up credits plus 7-day check-in credits, no card required. Starter Pass: 40 credits valid 7 days for $4.99. Subscriptions, monthly: Basic $11.90 (100 credits/month), Standard $29.90 (300), Pro slider $59.90 (750) up to $159.90 (2,300). Billed annually: Basic $118.80/year ($9.90/mo, 1,800 credits), Standard $238.80 ($19.90/mo, 4,800), Pro $358.80-$958.80/year ($29.90-$79.90/mo, 10,800-38,400). One-time packs, valid 6 months: 80 credits $9.90, 150 $19.90, 250 $29.90, 400 $39.90, 650 $59.90, 900 $79.90, 1,200 $99.90, 2,500 $199. Subscriber-only top-ups, valid 6 months: 300 $29.90, 1,500 $119, 4,500 $349, 8,500 $649, 12,500 $899. Per-generation cost is published per model on /pricing (GPT Image 2 3 credits/image, Nano Banana Pro 8, Seedance 2.0 Fast 50 credits per 5s, Seedance 2.5 125 per 5s, MiniMax H3 25 per 5s). Annual cards show 17%, 33% and 50% off the monthly equivalents and the site carries a standing '-50%' promo badge. USD. Verified 2026-11-10 on /pricing, /zh/pricing and the plan config shipped in the page.
best_for: E-commerce sellers, small marketing teams and creators who turn existing product shots into listing images, ads, mockups and social graphics without a designer - one browser workspace over GPT Image 2.5/2.6, the Nano Banana 2.x family, Seedream 5.0 and FLUX 3, with 30 free credits on sign-up and one-time packs from $9.90. A sensible fit if you want per-image credit control instead of a fixed subscription and will read the refund rule before paying: 3 calendar days, 50 paid credits or fewer, minus a 2-10% processing fee. Not a fit if you need to know who the data controller is, how long uploaded product photos are kept, or that your outputs are licensed for commercial use before you upload client material - no privacy notice on the site names a controller, address or retention period, training use is never mentioned, and the Terms decline to guarantee commercial usability even though the marketing copy says a commercial licence is included.
summary: Makify AI is a browser workspace for prompt-driven image editing and generation with a product-photography focus: upload a JPG, PNG or WebP up to 30MB, describe the change in plain English, and get product scenes, listing images, ads, mockups and infographics, exported at 1K or 2K and up to 4K on models that support it. The same credit balance buys short video, and the pricing page publishes the credit cost for each model and each 5-second clip rather than leaving it to be discovered at checkout. The site is a rebrand of AI GPT Image - it announces the change in-app and keeps 'AI GPT Image' as an alternate name in its structured data - and it runs on third-party models it names and disclaims affiliation with, including OpenAI's GPT Image line, Google's Nano Banana family, ByteDance's Seedream and Seedance, FLUX, Qwen, Kling and MiniMax. Pricing is unusually consistent for this category: the subscription ladder, the one-time pack ladder and the per-model credit costs reconcile with each other, and the 17%/33%/50% annual discounts match the monthly equivalents. What the site does not answer is who is accountable and how long uploads live. The footer names ARKELUMA LLC, but no privacy notice names a controller, address, jurisdiction or retention period, the Terms point governing law at 'the jurisdiction in which makifyai.com operates', training use is not mentioned anywhere, and analytics plus Microsoft advertising tags fire on first load with no consent banner rendered.

name: Midjourney
pricing: Paid plans
best_for: High-quality image generation and concept visuals
summary: A premium image-generation tool for brand visuals, concept art, moodboards, and campaign creative.

name: PawGroove
pricing: One-time credit packs only, no subscription and no auto-renewal, priced in USD: Starter $4.99 for 50 credits and Creator $9.99 for 120 credits, printed as $1.00 and $0.83 per 10 credits respectively. A dog video costs 10 credits, a full themed photo pack of 6-8 images costs 20, a 2-image preview costs 10, and extra image redos cost 3 credits each after two free redos per full pack. Eligible new accounts can receive 10 welcome credits for one video or a 2-image preview, not both, subject to network limits and a daily grant cap; trial videos are 480p and accounts with an eligible paid order get 720p for new videos. The same two pack prices, the same credit costs and the same per-10-credit figures appear on /pricing, on /zh/pricing and in the Terms, and the 50-credit and 120-credit pack arithmetic reconciles in the Terms' own examples ('50 credits can make two full photo packs and one video', '120 credits can make six full photo packs'). The live pricing page renders 'Buy Starter' and 'Buy Creator' buttons after its 'Checking payment availability...' placeholder resolves, and /api/config/public returns default_payment_provider:stripe, stripe_enabled:true and stripe_environment:live. No purchase was attempted.
best_for: Dog owners and pet creators who want a short vertical dance video, a themed photo pack or a custom sticker/GIF set made from one photo of their own dog - a Reel, Short or TikTok clip, a Christmas card photo, a sticker pack for a group chat - and would rather buy a small one-time credit pack than start another monthly AI subscription
summary: PawGroove turns one photo of one dog into a short vertical video, using a browser studio rather than an app. Its 11 templates are mostly solo routines and group scenes - Dog + Backup Dancers, Dog Trio Dance, Kung Fu Dog, a 90s Christmas movie, a Halloween zombie dance, a New Year dance, a five-second silent 'Scientists Reveal the Hi' clip - and the same balance also buys themed photo packs (6-8 images, including stickers and an animated GIF), custom transparent WebP stickers with your own words, and looping reaction GIFs. Most clips target about ten seconds at 9:16, start silent, and take an original PawGroove music track afterwards for free on supported templates, which the Terms license for use inside the video you post but not as a separate download. The library's examples are labelled 'Actual generated example' and are served as real MP4s; each template page prints its own input requirements and limits (one dog, paws visible, JPG/PNG/WebP up to 10 MB) rather than a shared marketing paragraph. It is a single-purpose consumer creative studio built on the ShipAny starter, with no subscription, no watermark claim and no account wall before you can see the price.

name: PawHeadshots
pricing: One-time only, no subscription: Superstar Pack $19.90 (36 ultra-HD images - 30 included looks plus 6 styles you pick - with Employee ID, PawkedIn profile and Pet Resume); Me & My Human Pack $29.90 (30 portraits of you with your pet, 30 transparent PNG cutouts, menswear or womenswear). USD; checkout adds local sales tax or VAT. Verified 2026-11-02 on the homepage pricing section and /studio.
best_for: Cat and dog owners who want a comedy headshot pack out of one phone photo - 30 fixed looks plus 6 styles you choose, with a matching Employee ID, PawkedIn profile and printable Pet Resume - as a single $19.90 one-time purchase; a $29.90 'Me & My Human' pack does 30 portraits of you and your pet together. Not a fit if you need to see the results before paying (there is no preview), if you expect the files to be stored for you (they are deleted 7 days after purchase), or if you need a company address and governing-law clause before you buy.
summary: PawHeadshots turns one photo of a dog or cat into 36 AI portraits: all 30 of its fixed comedy looks (Vacation Mode, Gym Bro, Shark Attack, Renaissance Noble and so on) plus six styles you choose, with a printable Employee ID, a PawkedIn parody profile and a one-page Pet Resume bundled in. A second pack renders 30 portraits of you with your pet in the same scenes. It is a novelty product, and the paperwork is unusually complete for a four-day-old domain: the operator is named as Vban LLC in both policies, every processor is named by company (Cloudflare for hosting, storage and order email; fal.ai running OpenAI and Google models; Stripe and Link as merchant of record), retention is given as periods rather than phrases, photos are explicitly excluded from AI training, and the pack carries commercial rights. The gaps are identity detail and buyer protection rather than honesty: no postal address, no jurisdiction and no governing-law clause, no /about, /contact, /cookies or /refund route, no preview before payment, and images that are deleted after seven days whether or not you downloaded them.

name: PawMambo
pricing: One-time credit packs only, no subscription and no auto-renewal, priced in USD: Try $6.99 for 60 credits (30 seconds of video), Make more $14.90 for 160 credits (80 seconds) and Keep creating $29.90 for 340 credits (170 seconds). The stated rate is 2 credits per second of finished video with a 10-credit minimum per request, so a 10-second clip is 20 credits, the built-in 16-second Denim Shuffle is 32 and a 30-second custom reference is 60; at those rates a 10-second video works out at $2.33 on the smallest pack and $1.76 on the largest. New accounts get 20 welcome credits once - enough for one 10-second video - and the page warns that a 16-second Denim Shuffle costs 32 credits, so the welcome grant does not cover it. Purchased credits do not expire. The pack arithmetic reconciles with the stated rate on every row (60 credits / 2 per second = 30 seconds, 160 = 80, 340 = 170), and the pricing page states the same figures in its FAQ answers. Stripe handles payment; no purchase was attempted.
best_for: Dog owners and pet creators who already have a clip of someone dancing and want their own dog's photo to follow that exact movement - a 10 to 30 second vertical clip for a Reel, Short or TikTok - and who would rather buy a small one-time credit pack per clip than start another monthly AI video subscription
summary: PawMambo is a single-purpose browser studio that turns one dog photo plus a dance video into a short vertical clip, using Kling 2.6 motion control through Kie AI rather than a text prompt. You pick one of two built-in dance references - Denim Shuffle at 16 seconds, Varsity Strut at 10 - or upload your own 3 to 30 second MP4 or MOV under 10 MB, add a JPG or PNG of one dog up to 8 MB, sign in with Google and generate. Output is 720 by 1264 portrait, and the two example MP4s the studio plays are real files of 16.1 and 10.03 seconds showing the finished anthropomorphic-dog result rather than the reference clips. It sells one-time credit packs at 2 credits per second of video with a 10-credit minimum, gives new accounts 20 credits once, returns reserved credits when a generation fails, and lets you download the MP4 or create a public share page. What sets it apart from the rest of the pet-video wave is how much it prints about its own uncertainty: the features section says sample results are still being tested, the motion section says the operator still needs to test how closely output follows the reference, the FAQ says cat photos can be selected but have not been tested - and after a review exchange on 18 November 2026 the Terms and Privacy notice put the refund, commercial-use and provider-training limits in writing instead of leaving them out.

name: RapAI
pricing: One-time credit packs only, no subscription, no auto-renewal, USD: Lite $6.90 / 390 credits, Pro $14.90 / 1,000 credits, Ultra $29.90 / 2,200 credits; credits valid 365 days from purchase. The stated generation cost is duration- and resolution-based: a 15-second clip costs 390 credits at 480p, 825 at 720p and 2,055 at 1080p, and the studio quotes a 5-second 480p render at 130 credits - exactly one third of the 390 figure, so the ladder is linear in duration. Every pack card reconciles against those numbers (Lite 390 = 1 x 15s 480p, Pro 1,000 = 2.56, Ultra 2,200 = 5.64, printed on the cards as 'about 1', 'about 2' and 'about 5' - conservative in the buyer's favour). Effective cost of a 15-second 480p video: $6.90 on Lite, $5.82 on Pro, $5.30 on Ultra; a 5-second 480p clip is $2.30 on Lite. The same three prices and the same three credit figures appear on /pricing and /zh/pricing. Failed generations return the task credits. Payment runs through Waffo - /api/config/public returns waffo_enabled:'true' - but the processor is named nowhere in the Privacy or Refund policy, which say only 'trusted third-party payment processors'. No purchase was attempted.
best_for: People who already have a photo of two people - a friend, a partner, a sibling, a team - and want a 4 to 15 second vertical rap performance generated from it for TikTok, Reels or Shorts, without filming, recording vocals or opening an editing timeline, and who would rather buy a one-time credit pack than a monthly AI video subscription
summary: RapAI is a browser studio that turns one photo of two people, or two separate portraits, into a short AI rap performance. You supply the photos and a background, then choose one of three rap modes - a surprise verse, a theme you describe, or your own lyrics - and pick a ratio, a duration of 4 to 15 seconds and 480p, 720p or 1080p. The site writes the bars when you do not, animates both performers to the generated vocals, and lists finished clips in your studio for download. It sells one-time credit packs at $6.90, $14.90 and $29.90 rather than a subscription, and it is unusual in this category for how specifically it writes down its own limits: photos are deleted from Cloudflare R2 seven days after upload with the period stated on the page rather than buried, SeeAPI is named as the generation provider, and a dedicated AI Technology Disclosure says the underlying model vendor and version 'have not been disclosed in the template documentation available to us' and that it 'cannot currently substantiate' any named foundation model. Commercial-use licensing is explicitly not offered, which is a real limitation for client work, and the site publishes no example video output at all - only still images - so a buyer cannot see what the result looks like before paying.

name: RapVideo AI
pricing: Free preview: some new accounts are offered one short low-resolution preview at the vendor's discretion (no card, no trial on paid plans). Monthly plans, credits reset each month and unused credits expire: Basic $29.90/mo (100 credits, shown on the card as 8 videos), Pro $49.90/mo (200 credits, 16 videos), Agency $99.90/mo (480 credits, 40 videos). Yearly plans renew automatically and are badged 'up to 44% off', but only the Basic yearly figure is in the served HTML ($299/yr for 120 videos, about 17% below monthly); Pro and Agency yearly prices need JavaScript. One-time packs, credits never expire: Single $9.99 (12 credits, 1 video), Trio $19.99 (36 credits, 3 videos), Crew $49 (120 credits, 10 videos), Studio $99 (300 credits, 25 videos), Label $199 (720 credits, 60 videos). A standard 12-second 720p render costs 10 credits; faster Seedance 2.0 tiers cost 8-20 and Seedance 2.5 Ultra up to 93 at 1080p. Failed, timed-out or safety-blocked renders are refunded automatically. USD, charged by Stripe.
best_for: People who want the Hotel Lobby / rap-duo trend video of themselves or a friend without filming anything, plus anyone making a birthday, anniversary, roast or small-business rap from two phone photos, who would rather buy credits per video than take on another monthly AI subscription
summary: RapVideo AI turns one or two uploaded photos into a short vertical rap video: it writes the lyrics around whatever topic you type, generates the beat and the vocals, and renders the people from your photos lip-synced on a stage you pick. The default Hotel Lobby (orange) stage in 'Original remake' mode recreates the real trend recording and choreography with your faces; the other stages make an original AI rap instead. Everything is paid in credits - 10 for a standard 12-second 720p render, more for the faster or higher-resolution Seedance models - either as one-time packs that never expire or as a monthly plan whose credits reset each month. Samples render in about two to three minutes, download as watermark-free MP4 in 9:16, square or widescreen, and a render that fails or is blocked by a safety filter is not charged. The site is a single-purpose studio built around this one job, with roughly 200 trend and guide pages around it.

name: RapVideoGo
pricing: One-time credit packs only, no subscription and no auto-renewal, credits never expire (the pricing bundle carries creditsValidDays: 0): Single $6.99 (10 credits), Duo Pack $29 (50), Crew Pack $99 (200), Studio Pack $199 (450), Label Pack $599 (1,500). The same five figures and the same 17% / 29% / 37% / 43% savings badges appear on /zh/pricing, and the pack SKUs in the shipped pricing chunk (rap_single 699c/10cr, rap_duo 2900c/50, rap_crew 9900c/200, rap_studio 19900c/450, rap_label 59900c/1500) agree with the cards. The studio shows the cost of the exact render before you commit: the default 9:16, 12-second, 480p render is priced at 24 credits, while every pack card estimates 10 credits per video. USD, charged through the site's own checkout after sign-in; /api/config/public returns waffo_enabled:true plus Google sign-in, email verification and password reset all enabled.
best_for: People who want a short rap video made from one or two phone photos of themselves, a friend or a colleague - the Hotel Lobby-style duet, a birthday or anniversary clip, a farewell for a coworker, or a friendly roast - and would rather buy a one-time credit pack than take on another monthly AI subscription
summary: RapVideoGo turns one or two uploaded photos into a short vertical rap video: you pick a template or write the lyrics, the site arranges the scenes and renders the people from your photos rapping to a generated beat and vocal. The default stage is a recording-studio duet, with a Hotel Lobby (golden lobby) effect, a rap-battle generator, birthday pages for a mother, friend, daughter, son, sibling or partner, plus anniversary, farewell and team-celebration templates. Output is 9:16 for TikTok, Reels and Shorts - the studio's default render is 12 seconds at 480p for 24 credits, and the sample clips on the page are 720p. Everything is bought as one-time credit packs that never expire rather than a subscription, and the site is explicit that only photos of consenting adults may be uploaded. It is a single-purpose studio with 70 indexed URLs (English plus a Chinese mirror) and eight how-to guides around it.

name: ReelBoop
pricing: Two ways to buy, both in USD and both metered per generation. Subscriptions: Creator $9.90/month for 200 credits, or $99/year for 2,400 credits shown as $8.25/month; Pro $29.90/month or $299/year for 9,600; Studio $59.90/month or $599/year for 24,000. Yearly allowances are released upfront and plan credits expire at the end of the billing period. One-time credit packs: $15 for 200 credits, $45 for 800 and $90 for 2,000, valid 365 days with no auto-renewal. Credit costs are printed per tool before you start: GPT Image 2.6 and Nano Banana 2.1 at 5 credits an image, Kling 3.0 Pro at 60 credits per 5-second clip, Seedance 2.5 at 100 credits per 5-second clip, and the product-film preset at 10 credits a generation. There is no free trial - the pricing FAQ says video generation requires credits. The annual discount is a flat ~17% on all three tiers ($99 against 12 x $9.90 = $118.80, $299 against $358.80, $599 against $718.80), the /zh/pricing mirror prints the same figures to the cent, and the refund policy restates the Creator monthly figure at $9.90 for 200 credits. Stripe handles payment; no purchase was attempted.
best_for: Creators who want a trending short video - a K-pop dance, a duet, an outfit change, a pet bit or a product film - assembled from one or two of their own photos, and who would rather buy metered credits than take on another full editing suite or a model API account
summary: ReelBoop is a trending-video studio: you pick a template from a catalogue of about sixty dance, duet, transformation, pet and product scenes, upload the one or two photos the template asks for, and get a vertical MP4 back. The catalogue is specific rather than generic - every card prints how many photos and how many seconds it needs, so 'LISA Tarantino AI Dance' reads '1 photo, 15s' and 'JISOO ADDICTED' reads '2 photos, 15s' before you commit. Underneath, different templates run different models, and the pricing page quotes each cost up front: Kling 3.0 Pro at 60 credits per 5-second clip, Seedance 2.5 at 100, Wan 2.2 I2V Fast for the product-film preset, and GPT Image 2.6 or Nano Banana 2.1 for stills. Generated clips land in private Cloudflare R2 storage with playback and download tied to the owning account, there is no public gallery, and a confirmed failed generation returns its reserved credits. Pricing is three metered subscription tiers or three one-time credit packs, with a 365-day expiry on pack credits and a 7-day refund window on an untouched pack. The parts that make it worth listing are the consent gate that actually blocks analytics until you accept, the per-model credit table, and the refund page - the parts a buyer should weigh are the missing operator identity and the absence of any free trial.

name: Retouchia
pricing: Free: 5 credits on sign-up (~1 image), no card required, full-resolution downloads. One-time packs only, no subscription: Basic $9.99 (shown against a $12 anchor, "Save 16%", 350 credits, advertised as ~70 images), Pro $29.99 (anchor $39.90, "Save 24%", 1,200 credits, ~240 images). Paid credits expire 365 days after purchase. Payment is processed by Waffo Pancake.
best_for: Ecommerce sellers, creators and small marketing teams who need occasional one-off photo edits - background removal, object removal, upscaling, old-photo restoration, colourising - and would rather buy a $9.99 credit pack than add another monthly AI subscription. Not a fit for anyone who needs a named legal counterparty, a contractual jurisdiction, or a guarantee about which specific model runs their image.
summary: Retouchia is a browser photo editor that puts several third-party image models behind one credits wallet. You upload an image, type an instruction such as "remove background", "erase object" or "enhance quality", choose a model and resolution, and download the result. It covers quality enhancement, deblurring, background and object removal, upscaling, old-photo restoration, scratch removal, colourisation, smart crop, black-and-white conversion and format conversion, with dedicated pages for upscaling, object removal, photo restoration and a GPT Image 2.5 landing page. There is a 5-credit free tier and two one-time packs - $9.99 for 350 credits and $29.99 for 1,200 - with no subscription, credits valid 365 days. Generation runs on third-party providers that the Terms name explicitly (APIMart and APIModels, serving SparkPix and Nano Banana 2), with prompt screening and output moderation before delivery, and failed or blocked runs restore the credits.

name: StylMorph
pricing: Free to try once: one successful Seedream 4.5 image per guest identity, no account, shared across the site's image tools. Then one-time credit packs with no subscription and no auto-renewal - Starter $6.99 for 40 credits ($0.175 per credit), Creator $12.99 for 90 ($0.144) and Studio $24.99 for 200 ($0.125) - and purchased credits never expire. Cost per image depends on the model: Seedream 4.5 is 1 credit, Nano Banana Pro is 4 purchased credits, and the fixed two-model comparison is 2 purchased credits, so a Seedream image is about $0.06 on the largest pack and a Nano Banana Pro image about $0.50. Nano Banana Pro and comparisons cannot be paid for with free or gifted credits. Checkout is by Stripe after Google sign-in, the cost is quoted before each generation, and results are downloadable for 24 hours. No purchase was attempted.
best_for: People who want one photo redrawn as comic art, a cartoon or a game-art frame without opening Photoshop - and who also want a free browser toolbox for crops, borders, watermarks and format conversions that never uploads the file
summary: StylMorph is a browser image transformer with a wider toolbox around it. The paid centre of it is an image-to-image tool: upload a JPEG, PNG or WebP up to 10 MB, pick an inked, halftone, cel-shaded, storybook or game-art treatment, compare the result against the original with a slider and download. Two models sit behind it - Seedream 4.5 at 1 credit an image and Nano Banana Pro at 4 purchased credits - plus a fixed two-model comparison for 2 credits, and a single free Seedream render per guest identity to test with. Around that it ships roughly thirty free browser-local utilities that the pricing page says do not upload your image at all: crop and straighten, add text, watermarks and borders, circle crops, rainbow profile frames, Instagram grids, colour-picker and palette tools, Base64 and metadata viewers, and JPG/PNG/WebP/AVIF converters. Pricing is three one-time packs whose per-credit prices reconcile exactly with the printed figures, credits that never expire, and results that expire after 24 hours on every plan. The privacy notice is the most specific in this batch - named analytics, a masked Clarity canvas, hashed addresses for quota, signed short-lived links - and the gap is where most of these sites leave it: no operator, no governing law, and no refund page beyond a 14-day clause for duplicate or undelivered charges.

name: TAROTAI.CHAT
pricing: Packs $2.99-$10.99 (one-time); subscriptions $3.99/mo and $9.90/mo
best_for: Drawing and interpreting tarot spreads in a chat interface, with follow-up questions inside a reading
summary: An AI tarot reader on its own 78-card Rider-Waite deck with upright and reversed meanings, four spread types, six reader personas and follow-up questions within a session. Credits are charged per spread and the credit cost of each spread is published.

name: TheFaceRating
pricing: Free on-device scan with no account. Paid reports are one-time purchases, not subscriptions: Starter USD 7.99, Pro USD 16.99, VIP USD 24.99, listed identically on the homepage plan cards, the results-page paywall and Terms section 6. Studio credit packs are stated in the Terms only - 10 credits for USD 9.99 and 30 credits for USD 19.99, one credit per rating plus render, credits do not expire. Checkout is a live Stripe session (verified 2026-10-24: cs_live session for 'TheFaceRating Starter Report' at USD 7.99, merchant Vban LLC, Apple Pay and Google Pay offered); applicable tax shows at checkout. Free AI colour analyses are capped at two per day per hashed IP address.
best_for: Anyone who wants a fast, private read on facial proportions before spending money on a haircut, a pair of glasses or a colour palette, and who reads the score as a styling starting point rather than a verdict on attractiveness. Also a useful sandbox: the Studio scores any reference photo against your own face. Not a fit for readers who want the rating to mean something objective, who need a working support mailbox before they pay, or who would rather not involve a face at all - the free scan keeps the photo on the device, but the colour analysis and every try-on require sending a compressed copy to the vendor and its model providers.
summary: TheFaceRating turns one selfie into a face rating. Google's MediaPipe face mesh places 478 landmarks in the browser, the site levels the head on the iris line and scores 11 proportions into a single 0-100 harmony number, then names the face shape across six prototypes and shows symmetry, canthal tilt, facial thirds and width-to-height ratio against a reference band. It also returns a celebrity bone-structure 'twin' as a percentage. The free scan needs no account, and we confirmed by running it that the measuring step sends nothing: landmarks, ratios and the result page are produced with no outbound request. The paid report adds 14 try-on renders on the buyer's own photo - six hairstyles, four necklines, four eyewear frames - plus a 12-season colour palette, a styling guide and, on Pro and VIP, a 30-day plan, a PDF and Studio credits for rating any look you find. Colour analysis is the one step that needs the photo, and the site asks for it with an unticked consent choice that can be declined while still returning full geometry results. Reports are sold by Vban LLC, a Wyoming company, under Wyoming law.

name: TryBestSpecs
pricing: One-time credit packs, no subscription: 10 credits USD 2.99, 30 credits USD 6.99 and 100 credits USD 14.99, each card showing a struck-through list price of USD 4.99 / 9.99 / 24.99. Credits never expire and each try-on costs 1 credit, so the packs buy 10, 30 or 100 generations; the per-credit arithmetic on the page reconciles (about USD 0.30, 0.23 and 0.15). Signup grants 1 credit, which is the entire free tier. The served plan payload marks every pack interval "one-time" with valid_days 0 and carries no recurring flag; the payment providers listed are Stripe and Creem. Verified 2026-10-25 from the rendered /pricing page and the plan payload embedded in it; the Chinese mirror /zh/pricing shows the same three packs at the same dollar prices.
best_for: Anyone picking frames online who wants to see a specific shape, colour and material on their own face before ordering, and who is willing to make an account and buy a small credit pack for a batch of renders. The middle pack is the one that makes sense if you plan to compare several styles. Not a fit for readers who want an anonymity-first try-on with no account and no stored history, who need a real fitting or prescription advice rather than a style preview, who want a free trial long enough to judge output on their own face, or who need a named company and a stated jurisdiction before paying.
summary: TryBestSpecs turns one selfie into a glasses try-on. The measuring step runs in the browser: the shipped bundle loads MediaPipe's FaceLandmarker with the GPU delegate, and its geometry feeds a face-shape classification (round, square, oval, heart, long, diamond) plus a skin-tone read that together drive the frame recommendations. Rendering the recommended frames onto your photo is a server-side AI step, and so is own-frame mode, where you upload a picture of frames you already own. Results land in an automatic history you can revisit, compare side by side, download in high resolution and share. Everything sits behind an account: signup grants 1 credit, each try-on costs 1 credit, and further credits come as one-time packs of 10, 30 or 100 that never expire. The interface, the guides and the legal pages are published in English and Chinese.

name: CCC (Claude Command Center)
pricing: Free: USD 0, with no tiers, no paid plan, no seat count and no account for the local app. Licensed FSL-1.1-MIT (copyright 2026 Amir Fish), which is source-available rather than OSI open source: you may use, copy, modify and redistribute it for any Permitted Purpose, a Competing Use is barred, and each version converts to the MIT license on its second anniversary. Downloads are a 3.6 MB notarized and Apple-signed DMG, a Homebrew tap (amirfish1/tap/ccc), a curl installer for macOS/Linux and a PowerShell installer for Windows. The optional CCC Cloud phone relay is account-based; no price appears for it on any fetched page either. No page on the site carries a price token other than $0.
best_for: Developers who already run several coding agents and keep losing track of them in terminal tabs. CCC is worth a look if you launch Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and friends from a terminal and want one local board that shows every session, which one is waiting on you, and which has quietly run out of context - without routing your work through someone else's cloud. It is not a fit for a single-session user (a terminal is enough), for anyone who wants a hosted team product with accounts and permissions, for a Windows or Linux shop expecting parity with the macOS app, or for a buyer who needs a company entity and a governing-law clause before installing software.
summary: CCC (Claude Command Center) is a local dashboard for people running several coding agents at once. Instead of owning execution, it reads each engine's on-disk state as the source of truth, so a session you started in a terminal, resumed by hand or launched headless outside the dashboard still shows up on the board - that is the difference between a dashboard and a second place you have to remember to work from. On top of the board it adds a needs-attention lane that flags sessions ending on a real question, a per-session context meter, plan-usage and rate-limit projections, a Kanban with a project tree and an infinite Flow canvas, group chats between agents, a work queue with verify-to-close receipts, git worktrees per task, and an optional fallback that keeps a limit-hit session running on a $0 model. The stack is deliberately plain: a stdlib-only Python server bound to 127.0.0.1 and a no-build vanilla-JS UI, with readable JSON state under ~/.claude/command-center/. Claude Code is first-class; Codex, Cursor, Antigravity, Kilo Code, Kimi Code, OpenCode and Devin spawn and ingest with documented gaps. Version 5.39.0 shipped 2026-10-18 and the repository was pushed the same day this review was written.

name: Reply Argus
pricing: No self-serve free plan is published on /pricing, which sells three monthly-or-yearly plans and Enterprise: Indie $9.99/mo or $99.90/yr ($8.33/mo billed annually) with 4 active apps and 300 replies/mo; Pro $19.99/mo or $199.90/yr ($16.66/mo) with 10 active apps and 2,000 replies, adding automation rules, auto-translate, analytics, the public REST API and signed webhooks; Studio $99/mo or $990/yr ($82.50/mo) with 30 active apps and 8,000 replies, white-label sending domain and per-app isolation; Enterprise custom. Every plan starts with a 14-day free trial and the card is required at signup: the pricing FAQ answers 'You add a card to begin, but nothing is charged until day 14'. Seats are included rather than sold (5 / 10 / 25 / unlimited) and viewers are free; the FAQ states 'You're never billed for overage'. Yearly billing is exactly ten months of the monthly price (2 months free), so 9.99x10 = 99.90, 19.99x10 = 199.90 and 99x10 = 990 all reconcile. The same three prices appear in /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt and the pricing page's JSON-LD Offer array. Two add-ons are described in the Terms (extra active-app slots billed on the regular cycle, and prepaid reply top-up packs that do not expire) but neither carries a price on /pricing. The vendor contradicts this on its own signup and login pages, which read 'Free for 1 app and 100 replies a month. You don't need a card', and the pricing FAQ answers 'Is there a free plan? No'. No purchase or trial was started; billing is by Dodo Payments as merchant of record.
best_for: iOS and Android developers, app studios and agencies who would rather answer App Store and Google Play reviews in the reviewer's own language than paste the same English template at every 1-star - especially teams that want an approval gate before anything posts to a store, and developers who want the review queue reachable from an AI agent over MCP or from their own read-only REST integration
summary: Reply Argus connects to App Store Connect and Google Play, pulls every review from both stores into one inbox, and drafts a reply in the reviewer's own language - 100+ languages, drawn from the app's own store listings, marketing page, past approved replies and any notes you add, with the cited lines shown so a draft can't invent a refund or a ship date. Nothing posts until you approve it; auto-publish is opt-in and can be scoped by rating, keyword, language or store, and on Pro and up a rules engine handles that. Alongside the inbox it clusters duplicated complaints with a match score and ranks recurring asks into a 'Signal' feed that can be exported to Notion or Sheets as a roadmap. Pricing is per reply volume rather than per seat: Indie $9.99/mo (4 apps, 300 replies), Pro $19.99/mo (10 apps, 2,000 replies, API and webhooks), Studio $99/mo (30 apps, 8,000 replies, white-label), each with a 14-day trial and a card at signup. For teams that want the queue inside an agent, /api/mcp is a remote MCP server signed in over OAuth, and /api/v1 exposes read-only apps and reviews with signed webhooks. The gaps a buyer should know about are documentary: no company, address or governing law anywhere on the site, no refund policy page, unnamed AI providers, and a signup page that advertises a free plan the pricing page denies.

pricing: Free $0: unlimited topic draws (1, 3 or 5 at a time from a 250-topic library in English, Chinese, French, Indonesian, Arabic, Turkish, Thai and Hindi), the 1/2/3/5-minute timer and local recording, with no account and no credits; free accounts cannot request the AI report. Standard $19.9 a month for 2,000 credits a month; Pro $59.9 a month for 6,000 credits a month (the page calls it 3x the monthly credits), both 'valid for the current month; cancel anytime'. One-time packs, 'one-time payment, no auto-renewal': $5.00 for 500 credits, $10.00 for 1,000, $20.00 for 2,000. AI analysis is 100 credits a run, so a $5 pack is about 5 analyses, $10 about 10 (the card itself says 'Up to 10 AI analyses (100 credits each)'), Standard about 20 a month and Pro about 60 - roughly $1 an analysis on every path. Paid by card through Stripe; the plan prices, credit allowances and Stripe price keys also appear in the shipped app bundle. USD. Verified 2026-11-14.
best_for: People practising impromptu speaking on their own terms - language learners, teachers running a class warm-up, Toastmasters-style clubs, and anyone who wants to talk for one minute without freezing. The free path needs no account: draw 1, 3 or 5 topics from a 250-topic library in eight languages, pick a 1/2/3/5-minute timer, and record locally. The paid path is only for the AI speech report, which costs 100 credits a run (about $1 on every pack and plan), so it fits someone who wants grammar, filler-word and pacing feedback and is willing to pay per analysis. It is not a fit if you need a named company, a governing-law clause or a published refund term before you subscribe, if you object to ad-supported pages on a paid product, or if you want a human coach - the report is model output scored on six fixed dimensions.
summary: Random Topic Generator is a speaking-practice site with a free half and a paid one. The free half does what the name says and needs no account: it draws 1, 3 or 5 topics from a library of 250 prompts in eight languages, filtered by everyday, work, creative or opinion, and pairs each pick with a one-, two-, three- or five-minute timer while the browser records you. The paid half is the AI report: upload the recording and get a transcript, a native-speaker rewrite, grammar corrections with explanations, pronunciation and clarity notes, filler-word counts, pacing and pauses, and tone - scored on six weighted dimensions (grammar 20, coherence 20, vocabulary 15, fluency 20, filler words 10, confidence) at 100 credits, about $1, per run. Topics can also be generated from a custom request after signing in with Google. The site runs two further free generators behind the same login - YouTube tags and job titles - and eight locale mirrors of the whole thing. Pricing is unusually coherent: the monthly plans, the one-time packs and the per-analysis credit cost reconcile to the same ~$1 on the pricing page, the Chinese mirror and the shipped plan config. The documents are the weak half - the Privacy Policy and Terms both say the service requires sign-in and offers no anonymous access, which is the opposite of how the free tier ships, and a recurring subscription is sold with no refund policy published anywhere.

Note Plus transcribes live inside the companion app, which is a third-party product called AI DVR Link; Note ONE transfers over Wi-Fi and generates the notes after upload. Year one is the cheap part of the AI cost on Note Plus, because the Max plan is included; from year two the free tier drops to 400 minutes a month and the paid ladder that applies to you is the thing to check before buying, since the two product pages currently quote different prices for it.

Not a fit for Android users (iPhone only), or for anyone who wants their notes to never leave the device - interpretation requires a server round-trip to Anthropic and OpenAI, which the policy states plainly.
summary: Dreamlock is a private dream journal for iPhone: record a half-asleep voice note, and the app transcribes it, writes a retelling with symbols and interpretation, and paints a dream card. Face ID locks the journal, there is no account to create, and iCloud sync is optional and encrypted. The data-flow disclosure is the standout: the policy names the exact pipeline (a small Vercel relay forwards the transcribed text to Anthropic's Claude for the writing and OpenAI's image model for the card, with only a scene description sent for the painting), states the data is never used for advertising or training, and accurately disclosed the two analytics scripts (cookieless Ahrefs and GA4) that we independently found in the page heads. The App Store page names the individual seller, and the terms set Delaware governing law. What keeps it below the top tier: it is a small new single-platform app, interpretation requires a server round-trip by design, and the seller is a natural person with no company structure.

name: FicWeave
pricing: Subscriptions only, in USD, plus a one-time free allowance rather than a trial. Free after sign-in: 3 starter credits that do not expire, 1 editable story, read-only Story Memory and up to one recent chapter of context. Pro $7.99/month for 100 credits per subscription month and up to 20 editable stories; Pro+ $14.99/month for 200 credits and 50 stories; Max $24.99/month for 400 credits and 100 stories. Annual billing charges once and grants credits monthly: $79.90, $149.90 and $249.90, which is exactly ten monthly payments and matches the 'Save 16.7%' badge on every card; the /zh/pricing mirror prints the same figures to the cent and the Terms restate both columns. A saved standard continuation costs 1 credit; a failed or cancelled attempt returns its reservation to its original source and expiry; Story Memory updates cost nothing. Subscription credits expire at each monthly window with no rollover, on annual plans too. One-time Credit Packs are no longer sold - /pricing, /terms, /refund-policy and /contact each say so - and only prior purchases keep their historical terms. All six SKUs (three plans x monthly/annual) report ready:true at /api/payment/checkout-readiness; the Choose buttons ship disabled in the served HTML and enable after the client-side account check. Waffo Pancake is the merchant of record for checkout, tax and the customer portal. No purchase was attempted.
best_for: Fanfiction and original-fiction writers who want a saved, chapter-by-chapter manuscript with a visible, source-linked memory of characters, relationships and open plot threads - instead of re-pasting a growing context into a chat window every chapter
summary: FicWeave is a single-purpose writing workspace for fanfiction. You give it a fandom or an original universe, the characters, a relationship or trope and a one-line what-if, and it writes a first chapter you can read without an account; saving the story creates a private library and a continuation workspace. Each continuation is assembled from selected Story Memory - Characters, Relationships, Important Facts, Open Threads and a bounded summary, with every AI-created item labelled by the chapter it came from - plus recent chapters (one on Free, up to six on paid plans). The claim being sold is workflow, not prose: the FAQ says outright that FicWeave 'does not promise better prose than ChatGPT or perfect continuity', and its own case-study page discloses an earlier failed extraction and a remaining continuity error rather than presenting a clean benchmark. All three paid plans run 'the same Pro writing model capability', so the ladder buys credits and editable-story slots rather than a better model. It is 18+, the Content Policy bans explicit sexual content and any sexualisation of minors or identifiable real people, and the Terms state that FicWeave is not affiliated with or endorsed by any fandom, franchise or author a user writes with.

best_for: Photographers, videographers and small studios who need one record of every camera, lens and drone - serials, receipts, values, loans and maintenance - instead of a spreadsheet beside a shared drive
summary: A camera-specific inventory and studio-operations app: every body, lens, filter, drone and accessory gets a record with serial number, purchase details, condition, storage location, photos, receipts and warranty files, plus loan status and service history. On top of that sit shoot planning with sun and weather, packing and readiness checks, QR labels and scan check-out, value trends and an insurance-ready PDF, and - on Studio - a client CRM, booking, quotes, contracts and invoices. An assistant called Iris answers questions about your own kit, including lens-to-camera mount compatibility, and a free browser tier covers 25 items with export on every plan.

name: Grammarly
pricing: Free + paid plans

summary: A writing assistant for grammar, tone, clarity, rewriting, and communication support across everyday business apps.

name: HtmlSlides
