best_for: Creating, playing, sharing, and embedding interactive HTML slide decks from a topic or brief
summary: An AI HTML presentation maker that turns prompts into interactive, browser-playable slide decks you can share, embed, and export as video.

name: HumanPen
pricing: Pay-as-you-go credits, one-time purchase, no subscription: 1,000 credits USD 19, 5,000 USD 79 (marked most popular), 10,000 USD 149, 20,000 USD 249. Every account's first purchase is discounted to USD 9.90 / 49 / 98 / 196 for the same four packs, once per account. New accounts get 100 free credits. Credits never expire and work in the web app and the API. Humanizing costs 100 credits per 1,000 words actually rewritten; citation-format correction is the cheapest operation at 5 credits per 1,000 words. Checkout runs through Waffo (the Privacy Policy also names Creem), each acting as merchant of record; prices are USD and no recurring plan is sold - the Terms state each purchase is a one-time charge.
best_for: Writers and researchers who already have a finished Word or PowerPoint file and need the file itself changed - AI phrasing reduced, references converted to a target style, a document cut to a word limit, or a layout-preserving translation - then downloaded again as an editable DOCX or PPTX. The unit of work is a whole document, not pasted text, so it suits a 50,000-word thesis with cross-references and figure numbering. Not a fit for anyone who wants a draft written for them (there is no generation entry point), for non-English humanizing, for assessed work where the institution restricts AI assistance, or for a buyer who needs a named company, country, postal address or a governing law that names a jurisdiction.
summary: HumanPen is a document toolbox that works on files rather than on a text box. You upload a DOCX or PPTX and get the same format back, edited: an AI-phrasing rewriter with two strengths that can import your own Turnitin or iThenticate report and touch only the flagged passages, a citation-format converter covering 12 styles, a shortener that hits a target word count, and a translator for 12 languages that keeps layout, charts and formulas. Billing is metered - you are charged for words actually rewritten, not for the whole file - and credits do not expire, so a 500-word job costs cents instead of a month's subscription. The humanizer is English-only and the vendor says so. There is also a documented REST API, an MCP server and an agent skill. The site is candid to an unusual degree about what the tool is for: the /ethics page states plainly that the humanizer is used to lower detector scores, declines to promise a pass, declines to run its own detector, and the Terms forbid submitting work as your own where an assessment requires independent work.

name: Microsoft Copilot
pricing: Free + paid plans
best_for: AI assistance across Microsoft 365, Windows, Edge, and enterprise productivity workflows
summary: Microsoft’s AI assistant for workplace productivity, search, writing, meetings, and enterprise software workflows.

name: Money Tracker (Expense & Budget)
pricing: Free with ads: manual entry, categories, budgets, charts, reports, multi-currency, split (AA) books and exports all work without paying. Premium is sold only inside the app stores - the vendor's own site publishes no price anywhere in its 45 locales. Apple's listing shows Yearly Premium $29.99 and Monthly Premium $2.99; Google Play lists in-app purchases at $2.99-$29.00 per item. Premium removes ads and adds unlimited AI entry, bill import (CSV, Excel, PDF or images), Android Smart Notification Entry, app lock, more books and accounts, and team books.
best_for: People who will log spending themselves - by hand, by voice, by photographing a receipt, or on Android by confirming a captured bank notification - and who want budgets and category reports without handing a bank login to an app. Fits solo users and small shared households that want one ledger, multiple currencies and split bills. Not a fit for anyone who needs a documented privacy notice covering financial data, a Terms of Service, or a named AI processor before installing a finance app.
summary: Money Tracker is a mobile expense tracker and budget app for Android and iPhone, published under the Google Play developer account Horoscope365 - the controller is a natural person, Zheng Kui, with a Beijing postal address on the Play developer block. You record income, expenses and transfers by hand, by voice ("lunch 12"), by photographing a receipt or bill, or on Android with Premium by confirming a transaction captured from banking or payment app notifications; Premium adds bill import, unlimited AI entry, app lock and extra books. Budgets can be set monthly and per category, with charts, category reports, multiple currencies, separate books, AA split ledgers and shared team books, and data exports to CSV, Excel or PDF. It deliberately does not link to a bank and never asks for bank credentials: without sign-in records stay on the phone, and signing in backs them up to the vendor's own server. Distribution is established rather than nominal - 5M+ Google Play installs at 4.8 stars from roughly 324K reviews, an App Store listing at 4.8 from 414 ratings, both updated in October 2026. The weakness is documentation, not the product: the marketing site publishes no price, links no legal page and prints no contact address, and the only privacy notice sits at an unlinked path that never mentions the financial data, receipt photos, voice clips or notification text the app handles.

name: Savingy
pricing: Free core with no card and no time limit: unlimited manual income and expense records, one-line entry, receipts, statement import, the tracker and money screens, monthly budgets and plans, goals and contributions, bill reminders, the Weekly Reset review, Ask Savingy, recurring purchases, calculators, and data backup/restore/export. Pro is sold as fixed access periods in INR, one payment each: Rs 149 for 30 days, or Rs 1,188 for 365 days - printed as about Rs 99 a month paid once, saving Rs 600 against twelve 30-day periods (12 x 149 = 1,788). No automatic renewal: the pricing FAQ answers 'Does Pro renew automatically? No. You pay once for 30 or 365 days. When the period ends, Pro stops and everything you logged stays on Free.' A one-time 45-day Pro trial opens after 30 real expense or income entries, at the user's choosing, with no card and no charge when it ends. Razorpay takes the payment; the shipped checkout bundle hardcodes the same amounts (monthly 149, yearly 1188) and loads checkout.razorpay.com/v1/checkout.js. The Google Play listing prints the identical offer: 'Rs 149 for 30 days or Rs 1,188 for a year. Fixed access periods: no subscription and no automatic renewal.' All prices include GST per the store listing. No purchase was attempted.
best_for: People in India who will log their own spending - by hand, one line, a receipt, a statement import or voice - and want one safe-to-spend number each day plus a forecast, without handing a banking password to an app; a sensible fit for anyone who would rather pay once for 30 or 365 days than start another auto-renewing subscription
summary: Savingy is an India-first expense tracker that turns what you log into one number - what is safe to spend today - plus a runway to month end, a monthly plan with budgets and goals, and a Sunday check-in it calls the Weekly Reset. Entry is manual by design: one line such as 'chai 40 upi', a receipt photo, a PDF, CSV or Excel statement import you review before anything is saved, or voice on Pro. There is no bank linking and it never asks for a banking password or PIN. The free core is not a trial - unlimited records, budgets, goals, the Weekly Reset, tracker history, reports and export cost nothing - and Pro is sold as fixed access, not a subscription: Rs 149 for 30 days or Rs 1,188 for 365 days, one payment each, with nothing renewing automatically. A one-time 45-day Pro trial opens after 30 real expense or income entries, at the user's choosing, with no card. The web app is the same product as the Android app on Google Play (com.rhnmaheshwari.savingy, updated 11 October 2026), which prints the same two prices and the same 'no subscription and no automatic renewal' line. The operator is Savingy Solutions Pvt. Ltd. (CIN U62013WB2025PTC282100), Tower House, 2A Chowringhee Square, Kolkata 700069, with Rohan Maheshwari named as director, and a Security & Trust Center that names its subprocessors - Microsoft Azure and MongoDB Atlas in Central India, Razorpay for payments, OpenAI for the assistant. The gap a buyer should know about is documentation drift rather than the product: the Privacy Policy and Terms still call the counterparty 'Savingy, Inc.', the December 2024 refund policy describes a renewing subscription the site does not sell, and the Terms still advertise Basic, Pro and Expert plans that do not exist.

A 14-day trial is advertised. This is property software with listing and lease tools, not a fair-housing or tenant-screening certification.

name: CrowdWisdomTrading
pricing: Free: weekly outlook email plus 20 free setups after signup, no card. Pay-as-you-go: $9.99 for 10 setup credits, one-time, no subscription. Pro: $29.99/month (taxes included at checkout) via Whop checkout, cancel anytime; yearly billing $179.99/year (advertised as 'saves 50%' against $359.88). Verified 2026-11-02 on /pricing.
best_for: Self-directed retail traders who want a curated second opinion: aggregated setups from experienced traders with entry, stop and target levels spelled out, plus a free weekly outlook to sample before paying. You still place the trade at your own broker - it never touches your money. Not a fit for anyone who wants execution, managed funds, or regulatory-grade advice; its own terms tell you to verify outputs with licensed professionals.
summary: CrowdWisdomTrading aggregates publicly shared views from experienced traders into daily and weekly research setups, each with an entry price, a stop and a target. It positions itself against Discord trading groups by grading every call in public, misses included, and it operates as research only - you execute at your own broker. The corporate disclosure is the best we have seen from a small submission in months: the terms name Tsuroni LTD as the operator, set Israeli governing law with Tel Aviv-Yafo courts, cap liability at a stated amount, and the privacy policy is drafted to GDPR/CCPA expectations with named retention logic for billing records. It loads no third-party trackers. The caution is the usual one for this product class: the 'pro traders' count and the public track record are self-published figures we cannot verify, and the terms themselves say the outputs are educational research, not investment advice.

name: 01Router
pricing: Pay-as-you-go credits, no subscription tiers: $1 = 100 credits. One-time packs are 1,000 credits for $10, 5,000 for $50, 10,000 for $100, 51,000 for $500 (+2% bonus), 103,000 for $1,000 (+3%) and 525,000 for $5,000 (+5%), all valid 365 days. Model rates are published per second, per image, per request or per 1M tokens - Seedance 2.5 runs from $0.055/second at 480p to $0.702/second at 1080p across nine providers, GPT Image 2.6 Flare from $0.016/image, GPT-6 Astra $2.66/1M input tokens. Signup grants starter credits; the homepage FAQ also promises a daily check-in bonus that the site's own public config reports as disabled. USD, no card for the free tier. Verified 2026-11-13.
best_for: Developers and small product teams adding AI video or image generation to an app who would otherwise need an account, API key and billing setup with several vendors, and who want to see each upstream provider's price before choosing a route. It also suits creators who want one credit balance across video, image, audio and chat in a browser studio, and agencies that want to resell the same models to their own users at a markup they set. It is not a fit if you need a named company, a governing-law clause, a refund policy or a training-use statement before you pay, if you need to buy more than $5,000 of credit at once, or if client media has to be covered by a processor you can name in a data-processing agreement.
summary: 01Router puts one API key in front of several model vendors. You post a model id and optionally a provider to /api/v1/generations, it forwards the job to whichever upstream serves that model - its own first-party route, AtlasCloud, APIMart, EvoLink, KIE AI, WaveSpeedAI, Replicate, fal.ai, Vercel AI Gateway or OpenRouter - and bills credits at 100 to the dollar. What makes the site worth reading is that it prints every upstream's price side by side for each model, so a buyer can see the spread before routing: the same Seedance 2.5 job costs $0.055/second on APIMart and $0.126/second on fal.ai at 480p. The pricing page lists 18 video, 18 image, 4 audio and 12 chat models while the model library page counts 37. Alongside the API there is a browser studio and playground, a bilingual English/Chinese build, and a Projects feature that lets you resell the same models to your own users at a markup you set. The commercial documents are thin: no company named anywhere, no governing law, legal pages dated six weeks before the domain existed, and no statement on training use of uploaded media.

summary: An image-to-video and text-to-video studio for product ads: it renders 3-15 second clips at 480p, 768p or 2K and charges credits per second of output, with a fixed credit cost per resolution. Packs never expire; subscriptions add monthly credits.

name: GatsbyAI
pricing: Lite $19.98/mo or $119.88/yr (2,000 credits a month); Pro $39.98/mo or $239.88/yr (5,000); Ultra $77.98/mo or $467.88/yr (10,000); one-time packs 1,500 credits $29.90, 3,000 $49.90, 5,000 $69.90, 8,000 $99.90; two free guest generations a day and 10 daily credits for a signed-in account
best_for: Generating short text-to-video and image-to-video clips across four model families from one browser workspace, with the credit cost of each run shown before you spend it
summary: A browser video generator that puts four model families behind one prompt box: Seedance 2.0 Mini, Kling, Veo 3.1 and the MiniMax H3/Hailuo routes. You type a scene or upload a first-frame image, set duration, aspect ratio and resolution, see the credit cost for that combination, and generate; an 'AI Optimize' step rewrites a weak prompt and suggests a model. Guests get two generations a day and signed-in accounts get 10 daily credits, then subscription or purchased credits take over, with generation history in the account and MP4 downloads. Failures release the reserved daily credits and return charged credits rather than consuming them.

name: Genjutsu AI
pricing: Free tier: 18 one-time signup credits, watermarked previews and downloads, roughly 3 images or 1 short clip, plus a weekly check-in worth up to 60 credits across the reward cycle. Subscriptions billed monthly: Starter $29.9 for 800 credits/month, Pro $49.9 for 1,800, Business $99.9 for 4,000. Billed yearly (the price printed on the card): Starter $100.0 a year, shown as $8.3/month, 2,400 credits/year; Pro $360.0 a year, shown as $30.0/month against a struck-through $49.9, 21,600 credits/year; Business $599.0 a year, shown as $49.9/month against a struck-through $99.9, 48,000 credits/year. One-time packs under the Pay once tab, credits never expire: Flex $99 for 2,000 credits, Starter Pack $199.9 for 4,900, Pro Pack $499.9 for 19,900. Subscription credits expire each period; card prices are USD before tax. Refund requests within 72 hours, calculated pro rata on unused purchased credits minus actual non-returned processing fees capped at 6% of the order. Read on 2026-10-26 from the rendered /pricing page on all three tabs; the plan figures are not literals in the served HTML, so they were captured from the rendered page rather than a price-token sweep.
best_for: Creators making trend-shaped short video who already have a performance worth copying and photos of the people, pets or products to put in it - the preset library does the prompt work and the workspace shows a credit estimate before you generate. Good fit for a two-person duet, a pet dance, a car or product swap, or a group scene where each photo has a labelled role. Not a fit for anyone who needs a named company, a stated jurisdiction and a retention period before paying, for work where an exact likeness or an unchanged background is contractual, for text-to-video alone (the AI Video Maker page covers that at a much higher credit cost), or for anyone unwilling to upload photos of real people to an unidentified operator.
summary: Genjutsu AI is a browser workspace for rebuilding a clip with different people, pets or products. You pick a trend preset from a library of dances, sporting moments, cinematic scenes and pet bits, or upload your own 4-30 second reference video, then add photos for the roles you want to replace; the site calls the two modes motion transfer and object swap. Generation runs on third-party video models - Kling 2.6 and 3.0 Motion Control, Wan 2.2 Animate Move and Animate Replace, Seedance 2.0 and 2.5 - with image models covering the still half of the site, and one credit balance pays for both. Google sign-in grants 18 starting credits (about three images or one short clip) with watermarked downloads; subscriptions run $29.9-$99.9 a month billed monthly, or $100-$599 a year, and one-time packs of 2,000 / 4,900 / 19,900 credits do not expire.

name: Marigold Pet
pricing: Single price, no tiers and no subscription: USD 6.99 one-time for one 15-second video (portrait 9:16 or landscape 16:9, one of four preset looks, AI-generated synchronised audio, MP4 download). No free tier or trial; the page's samples are the vendor's own renders. Checkout is hosted by Waffo Pancake as merchant of record; applicable tax is shown before payment. The site's own public config endpoint returns price 6.99, currency USD, billing one-time, mode prod - matching /pricing and the homepage.
best_for: Pet owners who want a finished, shareable Halloween video of their own animal and would rather pay $6.99 once than learn a prompt box or a video editor. The preset-look model is the point: four costumes, two aspect ratios, no free-form prompt, no timeline. Not a fit for anyone who wants to direct the scene, needs more than one video for the money, wants a free trial before paying, or needs a named company, postal address or contractual jurisdiction to buy from.
summary: Marigold Pet makes one thing: a 15-second Halloween video of your pet from a single photo. You upload a clear JPG/PNG/WebP up to 10 MB, pick one of four preset looks - pumpkin, witch, vampire or friendly ghost - and either 9:16 or 16:9, pay $6.99 once, and get an MP4 with a three-beat structure (arrival in a Halloween scene, magical costume reveal, hero pose) plus AI-generated synchronised audio. There are no prompts to write and no editing step. Costume stills run on Google Nano Banana 2 and the video and audio on MiniMax H3 Max Turbo, both through fal.ai; each finished video passes the provider's safety checker before delivery. The site is bilingual (English and Spanish) and the interface, pricing and legal pages are served in both languages.

name: Pika

A standard template generation costs 10 credits; the Baby Lip Sync template costs 30. Failed generations return the credits used. Checked 2026-11-03 on https://reeltada.com/pricing.
best_for: Social video creators who want to turn one or two photos into a trend-shaped vertical short for TikTok, Reels or Shorts without filming or editing - pick a live template, upload, download. One-time credit packs mean no subscription hangs over you. Not a fit for anyone who needs a named company, published retention terms or a stated model provider before uploading photos, or for professional editing work (no timeline editor, no developer API).
summary: ReelTada turns one or two photos into a ready-to-post vertical video using trend-ready AI templates for TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts. It sells only one-time credit packs - no subscription - and returns credits when a generation fails, which the refund policy states in writing. The legal set exists (privacy, terms, refund) and the content rules in the terms are unusually specific. The weaknesses trail the trend-microsite class: no operator identity or jurisdiction anywhere, the privacy policy names no processors, no retention period and no training-use statement, three analytics scripts load on every page (Plausible, Cloudflare Insights, and a self-hosted script from analysis.gaolong.site) with none of them named in the policy, and its own refund policy still calls the product 'Bby Wow' - a template leftover from another brand.
